tellings.quote: Beginning in 1973, I had sought out and interviewed former or retired US Air Force personnel who had either operated or guarded nuclear weapons, regarding their personal UFO encounters at ICBM launch facilities, missile warhead/bomb storage depots, and other nukes-related sites.
As of 2023, 167 USAF veterans and other military personnel have gone on-the-record for me and UFOs and Nukes is essentially a compilation of some of those individuals’ tape-recorded testimony.

plain: The journalist Robert Hastings has spent decades interviewing Air Force veterans who say UFOs showed up at American nuclear weapons sites, hovering over missile silos, tampering with communications and even shutting missiles down. His book of those accounts is UFOs and Nukes, whose first edition came out in July 2008. Michels cites it constantly, usually saying Hastings has 167 witnesses, men with Q clearances, the high security clearance needed for nuclear work, and describing objects shaped like Tic Tacs (white ovals like the mint), saucers and orbs; at times he says almost 170, once over 60, and says sightings were reported at every US nuclear base and abroad. Hastings himself corrected one detail by email, Michels says: only about 12 to 15 were radar operators, and the rest were missile security staff. If true, it would mean whatever is behind UFOs has a steady interest in nuclear weapons. In a 2024 article Hastings writes that "beginning in 1973" he sought out veterans who "had either operated or guarded nuclear weapons," and that "as of 2023, 167 USAF veterans and other military personnel have gone on-the-record," which dates the interviews from the 1970s, where Michels sometimes says the 1960s. A guest named John Blitch also praises the book on the show.
